what: Does the C-Mod era shift's attribution collapse survive matching the label prior of the explained set?
why: The worked example in README.md carries a label-prior shift (source 0.5085 positive, target 0.7208) alongside its covariate shift. Until 2026-09-26 the README said QFC does not separate the two. It has now been separated by measurement, so the README states the result instead of the caveat.
pre_registration: PLASMA_LABEL_PRIOR_PREREGISTRATION.md (outcomes P-HOLDS / P-VANISHES / IMMATERIAL / P-UNDERPOWERED fixed before the run)
provenance_note: Run with the research pipeline that produced the paper's own plasma numbers, on the SAME frames this package's demo builds (source 3,363 rows / 40 shots, target 2,504 rows / 38 shots, 48 features), NOT with this package. The two implementations differ slightly on the same data: this package reports QFC 0.9607, the research pipeline 0.9637 on its matched cap rule. The control is a comparison BETWEEN ITS OWN TWO ARMS, so that offset does not enter it.

held_fixed: the source model (RF 500 trees, depth 20, class_weight=balanced)
the source arm (GroupKFold-5 out-of-fold TreeSHAP over the source pool)
design.the_one_variable: the label composition of the 500 explained target rows
design.why_arm_T_exists: so that 'stratified rather than unstratified draw' is not a second changed variable; both arms are stratified draws of exactly 500 rows and differ only in composition
design.pairing: the same seed drives the source cap and both target draws, so the per-seed difference is paired

result.outcome_meaning: |paired delta| is SMALLER than the paired across-seed spread, which is the pre-registered strongest form of 'the collapse survives'. The resolution 0.004958 is 5.6x below the pre-registered underpowered threshold of 0.0276 (the gap between the published real value and its null mean), so the design could have seen an effect this size and did not.

considered_and_not_built.idea: expose the control as an API option, e.g. screen(source_df, target_df, match_prior=True), so a user can run it on their own campaigns
considered_and_not_built.why_not: screen() answers one question -- does this model rely on the same features in both environments -- and a prior-matched arm answers a different one, whether an observed collapse is carried by the label composition of the explained sample. Folding the second into the first would make the primary verdict depend on a choice the user did not know they were making. It belongs as a separate diagnostic if a maintainer wants it, not as a flag on the entry point.
considered_and_not_built.what_a_maintainer_would_need: the arms are 20 lines: stratify the explained target sample to each prior in turn, hold everything else fixed, pair by seed. closure_scripts/plasma_prior_matched_qfc.py is the reference implementation and is readable as a spec.
considered_and_not_built.recorded_because: a design decision that leaves a capability out is worth stating; silently omitting it looks like it was not considered

limits: Both arms draw STRATIFIED samples, so neither z equals the -4.86 the paper reports for this condition under an unstratified random draw. The comparison that matters is between the arms, which share everything but composition.

The control changes the composition of the EXPLAINED set, not of the TRAINING set: the forest is fitted on the source pool at 0.5085 throughout, which is what the deploy-once protocol describes. A model retrained under the target's prior is a different question this design does not ask.
One shift pair exists in this public release, so nothing here generalises to other campaigns or machines.
